NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under City Council Meeting agendas at rhe.city and during regular
  business hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's website and a
  recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP-TV Channel 35
  (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome in-person on any item during City Council consideration of the item. Public
  correspondence may also be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record. Members of the public may also comment online using
  eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos” page of the City’s website
  (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment” button next
  to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After you
  register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
  public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the record.

  An opportunity is also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If
  you would like to address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public
  comment, please complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  OCTOBER 10, 2023

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR HUFF called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Los Angeles County Sheriff Deputy Derek Clotworthy.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  Stegura

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING OCTOBER 2023 "BREAST CANCER AWARENESS
  MONTH"

MAYOR HUFF declared September 2023 Breast Cancer Awareness Month.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

City Clerk Pettit, noted an error in item 5C, City Council Minutes of September 26, 2023.
The motion should reflect that COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA made the motion, and

A.  APPROVE AMENDED AND RESTATED AGREEMENT BETWEEN TURBO DATA

  TURBO DATA SYSTEMS, INC. AND THE CITIES OF RANCHO PALOS

  PROCESSING PARKING CITATIONS AND IDENTIFYING THE THREE
  CITIES AS THE PALOS VERDES PARKING AUTHORITY AND AUTHORIZE

No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

D.  PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST -
  PEDESTRIAN CROSSING CONCERNS

  Recommendation: That the City Council direct staff to: 1) Remove the “Turning Vehicles
  Yield to Pedestrians While Turning Right” signs on the southwest corner of PVDN &
  PVDE; and 2) Install two new “No Right Turn on Red” signs as shown in the attached
  Exhibit A.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER described a video presented at the Traffic & Safety
Committee meeting that showed cars rolling through the right turn at the intersection without
stopping, one after another for over an hour. She also emphasized that it is not only children
who are of concern at this intersection, but also equestrians. Lastly, she noted that on page 5
of the staff report, data shows that there would not be a significant back up of cars with these
proposed signs added.

Public Works Director Wahba stated that staff has discussed additional monitoring to ensure
compliance at this intersection by the Lomita Sheriff Station, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM
SCHMITZ. MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ emphasized the importance of educating people
about this change.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
Public testimony was received by residents John Owens, Maddock Su, and Lynn Yen, all in
support of the recommendation. Another resident, John, expressed concern about this signage
leading to people cutting through the Nature Center parking lot to make the right turn without
having to wait for the signal.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Joanne Itagaki added that the school is trying to re-start the walking
school bus, and that there is a sign on PVDE just before the access point to the Nature Center.
Future plans for the Nature Center will include considerations to discourage people from cutting
through the parking lot, including possible speed humps.

MAYOR HUFF thanked Joanne Itagaki for her years of service to the City and congratulated
her on her upcoming retirement.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
OCTOBER 10, 2023
   COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  DIRECT STAFF TO: 1) REMOVE THE “TURNING VEHICLES YIELD TO
  PEDESTRIANS WHILE TURNING RIGHT” SIGNS ON THE SOUTHWEST
  CORNER OF PVDN & PVDE; AND 2) INSTALL TWO NEW “NO RIGHT TURN
  ON RED” SIGNS AS SHOWN IN EXHIBIT A.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Stegura

9.  OLD BUSINESS

None.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

None.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

A.  CALIFORNIA CONTRACT CITIES ASSOCIATION'S ANNUAL SACRAMENTO
  LEGISLATIVE TOUR JANUARY 8 - 10, 2024

All Council Members plan to attend the Sacramento Legislative Tour. City Manager Grammer
added that Assistant City Manager Davis and Management Analyst Slawson will also be
attending.

MAYOR HUFF announced that the Tracy Austin Doubles Tennis Tournament would be held
this weekend at Ernie Howlett Park and the Jack Kramer Club, and the Prepared Peninsula
Expo will be held October 22 at 10:00 am at Peninsula High School. In conjunction with the
Prepared Peninsula Expo this year, Assemblymember Al Muratsuchi and Senator Ben Allen
will host a Natural Disaster Town Hall along with the California Department of Insurance that
day at 1:00 pm.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL-ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Section 54956.9(d)(2)
  Significant exposure to litigation: one case

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 7:40 p.m. MAYOR HUFF adjourned the City Council meeting in memory of Manhattan
Beach Police Officer Chad Swanson. The meeting was adjourned to Tuesday, October 24,
2023, at 7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a Regular Meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Britt Huff
City Clerk  Mayor
